title: Introduce sentinel scoring hook with composite thresholds and incremental prompt targeting
author: Maya Patel
ci_status: pass (one flaky test rerun required - tests/test_sentinel.py flaky on first run, rerun succeeded)
description: Motivation: reduce noise and CI cost from full-suite prompt regressions while preserving high-fidelity gating for production rollouts. This PR adds a new CI hook (sentinel) that computes a composite regression score per-prompt-set and enforces configurable actions (fail/warn/annotate/autosnooze) based on multiple signals: stability_score (historical variance-weighted delta), worst_prompt_delta (largest single-prompt regression), and percentile_regression (p90/p95 aggregated drop). The sentinel is designed to be lightweight: it targets only the minimal incremental cohort affected by a change (changed prompt files, changed examples, or tagged cohorts), uses cached evaluation artifacts when available, and falls back to full-eval only when necessary. Implementation summary: Added eval/orchestrator/sentinel_hook.py which contains the scoring pipeline and threshold evaluation; added configs/sentinel.yaml to expose tuning knobs (weights for composite score, per-cohort thresholds, autosnooze window); integrated the hook into CI via ci/hooks/pre-merge-sentinel.yml that runs after unit/integration tests but before merge; implemented incremental target discovery in eval/utils/changed_prompt_detector.py which leverages git diffs and prompt metadata; added unit and integration tests under tests/test_sentinel.py and tests/integration/test_sentinel_in_ci.py; updated docs in docs/eval/sentinel.md with tuning guidance and example Linear workflows. Operational notes: default policy is conservative: p95 regression > 2.5 points OR worst_prompt_delta > 5 points -> fail; otherwise warn. Autosnooze can be enabled per-branch (useful for upstream model changes where team wants to temporarily silence gating while investigating). Performance: on typical PRs this reduces CI eval workload by ~2.5x vs full eval and dropped median CI eval time from ~18m to ~5m in our canary runs. Rollout plan: start as opt-in in dev teams, monitor false-positive rate and tune composite weights, then flip to default for main after 2 weeks of telemetry. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-1934) [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] docs updated [x] Linear task created for rollout (PM-442) [x] telemetry events emitted (sentinel.trigger, sentinel.decision, sentinel.reason_detail). Backward compatibility: sentinel is additive and disabled by default via sentinel.enabled=false; when enabled it can be configured to only annotate instead of blocking. See release notes below for user-facing changes.

review_comments: Alex Kim: Can the sentinel run concurrently with the existing cohort prioritizer or will it replace it? Author: sentinel currently composes with the prioritizer; it only selects the minimal target set and delegates ordering to the existing prioritizer.
Alex Kim: Suggest adding a backoff for autosnooze if repeated upstream model bumps occur. Author: added autosnooze.window and autosnooze.backoff in configs and documented recommended values.
Jordan Li: CI job time looks great; can we gate the sentinel run behind a 'fast-path' label on PRs? Author: added support for sentinel.skip-label to allow teams to opt-out per-PR.
Priya Raman: Please ensure telemetry exposes per-cohort false-positive counters. Author: added sentinel.telemetry.fp_count and included examples in docs.
Jordan Li: Approve after tests pass and flaky fixed. Alex Kim: Approve.

release_notes: Add a configurable 'sentinel' CI eval hook that computes a composite regression score (stability/percentile/worst prompt) and enforces actions (fail/warn/annotate/autosnooze). Disabled by default; see docs/eval/sentinel.md for configuration and rollout guidance.
diff_snippet:
@@ eval/orchestrator/sentinel_hook.py +1,15 @@
+def compute_composite_score(history, current):
+    stability = historical_variance_weighted_delta(history, current)
+    worst = max_per_prompt_delta(history, current)
+    p95 = percentile_regression(history, current, 95)
+    return cfg.weights.stability*stability + cfg.weights.worst*worst + cfg.weights.p95*p95
notes_on_testing: Canary on infra-dev: 42 PRs over 48 hours, sentinel annotated 6 and blocked 3 (teams confirmed 2 were true regressions). Flaky test encountered once due to async waiter; switched to event-driven approach and reran CI. Integration tests include simulated model bump scenarios and autosnooze flows.
implementation_risks: Potential risk is tuning sensitivity; defaults are conservative. Another risk is cached artifacts staleness - implemented TTL and cache invalidation on prompt changes.
how_to_enable: Set configs/sentinel.yaml -> enabled: true in your repo-level eval config or add 'sentinel: enabled=true' to CI variables. Use sentinel.thresholds.* to tune behaviour. See docs/eval/sentinel.md for examples.
notes_for_release_automation: Add a toggle in rollout playbook to monitor sentinel.telemetry.* and false_positive_rate metric for 2 weeks post-rollout. Add CI job badge showing sentinel status.
user_visible_changes: UI/PR annotations when sentinel warns/fails; new telemetry events visible in Console under 'Eval -> Sentinel'. Default disabled so no immediate user impact.
migration_guidance: No migration required. To migrate from current fuzzy gating, enable sentinel in a single repo and run with mode=annotate for 1 week to collect telemetry before switching to blocking mode.
canary_results_summary: Median eval time 18m -> 5m, compute tokens decreased ~20%, false-positive rate observed 4.8% on canary sample of 42 PRs.
